:::{#def-partial-derivative}
#### Partial derivative

Let $f : \reals^p \to \reals$ and $\vx = \tp{(x_1, \ldots, x_p)} \in \reals^p$.
The **partial derivative** of $f$ with respect to $x_j$ at $\vx$ is

$$
\deriv{x_j} f(\vx) \eqdef
\lim_{h \to 0} \frac{f(x_1, \ldots, x_j + h, \ldots, x_p) - f(x_1, \ldots, x_p)}{h},
$$

when this [limit](calculus.qmd#def-limit) exists.
It is the [derivative](calculus.qmd#def-derivative) at $x_j$
of the one-variable function $t \mapsto f(x_1, \ldots, t, \ldots, x_p)$,
which varies the $j$th coordinate and holds the other coordinates fixed.

:::
